selection_policy: Explicit F600-F2 train-only; disjoint from S600-common-400 families/snapshots/instances; normalize eligible only.

mechanism_evidence.contract: save_preprocessed owns a per-file working copy: the working gaze_df is not (is not) the caller GazeDataFrame; csv unnest/drop of the working copy leaves the caller frame untouched; captured at the save_preprocessed per-file loop-iteration timepoint.
mechanism_evidence.trigger: Save a gaze dataset with nested pixel/position/velocity/acceleration columns to csv, then keep preprocessing the in-memory frames.
mechanism_evidence.base_wrong_behavior: The loop variable aliases the caller GazeDataFrame; csv unnest/drop mutates the caller frame in place.
mechanism_evidence.causal_change: gaze_df = gaze_df.copy() at the loop top; GazeDataFrame.copy() preserves n_components.

discriminating_observation.description:
import tempfile
import polars as pl
from pymovements.dataset.dataset_files import save_preprocessed
from pymovements.dataset.dataset_paths import DatasetPaths
from pymovements.gaze.gaze_dataframe import GazeDataFrame
df = pl.from_dict({'t': [1000, 1001, 1002], 'x': [0.1, 0.2, 0.3], 'y': [0.1, 0.2, 0.3]})
gaze = GazeDataFrame(data=df, pixel_columns=['x', 'y'])
cols_before = list(gaze.frame.columns)
print('cols_before', cols_before)
paths = DatasetPaths(root=tempfile.mkdtemp(), dataset='ds')
fileinfo = pl.DataFrame({'filepath': ['f.csv']})
save_preprocessed(gaze=[gaze], fileinfo=fileinfo, paths=paths, verbose=0, extension='csv')
print('cols_after', list(gaze.frame.columns))
assert list(gaze.frame.columns) == cols_before, 'side effect: caller frame mutated'
print('f2_save_isolation', True)

triple.is_identity: working gaze_df is not the caller GazeDataFrame (per-file owned copy)
triple.shared_mutation_visibility: csv unnest/drop on the working copy stays invisible to the caller frame (assert_frame_equal in F2P)

mechanism_evidence.contract: Each kernel owns its activity map: a per-kernel map is not (is not) another kernel map nor the global defaults; publishing activity for one kernel leaves defaults and other kernels untouched; captured at the get_map_for_kernel access timepoint.
mechanism_evidence.trigger: Track two kernels (or query an unknown kernel id), then publish activity for one.
mechanism_evidence.base_wrong_behavior: Unknown-kernel queries return the single shared dummy_map object; mutations through it leak across kernels and the defaults.
mechanism_evidence.causal_change: Unknown kernels get DEFAULT_ACTIVITY_VALUES.copy(); each tracked kernel gets its own DEFAULT_ACTIVITY_VALUES.copy().

discriminating_observation.description:
from kernel_gateway.services.activity.manager import (
    ActivityManager, DEFAULT_ACTIVITY_VALUES, BUSY)
am = ActivityManager(['k1'])
m1 = am.get_map_for_kernel('k1')
m2 = am.get_map_for_kernel('k2')
print('identities', m1 is m2, m1 is DEFAULT_ACTIVITY_VALUES, m2 is DEFAULT_ACTIVITY_VALUES)
assert m1 is not m2
assert m1 is not DEFAULT_ACTIVITY_VALUES
assert m2 is not DEFAULT_ACTIVITY_VALUES
m1[BUSY] = True
assert DEFAULT_ACTIVITY_VALUES[BUSY] is False
assert m2.get(BUSY) is False
print('f2_kernel_isolation', True)

triple.is_identity: per-kernel map is not another kernel map nor the global DEFAULT_ACTIVITY_VALUES
triple.shared_mutation_visibility: publishing to one kernel stays invisible to defaults and other kernels
